approved: Telecommunications Legislation Amendment (Triple Zero Custodian and Emergency Calling Powers) Bill 2025
Infrastructure, Transport, Regional Development, Communications, Sport and the Arts
Written by a model from the explanatory memorandum; not the record
The bill would create a statutory role for a Triple Zero Custodian to oversee the end-to-end emergency call service.

The Custodian could ask the Australian Communications and Media Authority to direct carriers, service providers and emergency call persons to provide information or take action affecting the emergency call service.
The bill also harmonises the definition of 'emergency services' across two telecommunications Acts.
Establish the Triple Zero Custodian as a legislative position within the department.
Give the Custodian power to request ACMA directions on emergency call service matters.
Strengthen ACMA's ability to require information and direct action during outages and routine operations.
Introduce a formal information use and disclosure regime for the Custodian and ACMA.
Set reporting and review mechanisms for ACMA with ministerial oversight.
Align the definition of emergency services in the TCPSS Act and the Telco Act.
Carriers, carriage service providers, emergency call persons, the Australian Communications and Media Authority, the Minister for Communications, and the department.

The majority voted against [amendments](https://www.openaustralia.org.au/debate/?id=2025-10-08.24.2) introduced by Lindsay MP [Melissa McIntosh](https://theyvoteforyou.org.au/people/representatives/lindsay/melissa_mcintosh) (Liberal), which means they failed. Ms McIntosh [explained that](https://www.openaustralia.org.au/debate/?id=2025-10-08.24.2): > *The first point in my amendment seeks to list our triple 0 network as critical infrastructure. The majority voted against [amendments](https://www.openaustralia.org.au/debate/?id=2025-10-08.27.1) introduced by Mallee MP [Anne Webster](https://theyvoteforyou.org.au/people/representatives/mallee/anne_webster) (Nationals), which means they failed. Ms Webster [explained that](https://www.openaustralia.org.au/debate/?id=2025-10-08.27.1): > *These amendments ensure that the Triple Zero Custodian is reporting to the government and the parliament on the specific connectivity issues that rural, regional and remote Australians are facing.* ### Amendment text > *(1) Schedule 1, item 7, page 5 (line 33), at the end of subsection 151A(2), add:* > >> *; (c) the deficiencies in connectivity in rural, regional and remote Australia that put Australians living there at risk from ECS outage events.* > > *(2) Schedule 1, item 7, page 16 (after line 16), after paragraph 151Q(1)(b), insert:* > >> *(ba) the specific challenges and personal safety risks faced by Australians living in rural, regional and remote areas through poor connectivity to emergency call services;*

Argued that the emergency call service legislation was rushed after a 13-hour Optus outage affecting South Australia, Western Australia and the Northern Territory, during which more than 600 calls failed to connect and four people died; called for an independent review, greater transparency, and stronger accountability for Optus, the regulator, the department and the minister.

Moved amendments proposing $40 million civil penalties for specified telecommunications contraventions, argued for public outage registers and more frequent reporting, and pressed for transparency over Triple Zero outages. The minister said telcos would publish outage information on their own websites, the registers would be established through standards by the end of the year, and a letter to ACMA was tabled.
